title: Delhi HC: Can't Keep the Favourable Parts of an Award From an Invalid Arbitrator
case_name: Life Insurance Corporation of India v. N.S. Associates
card_summary: LIC's own Executive Director had unilaterally appointed the sole arbitrator in 2019, and a Single Judge already found that appointment impermissible under Section 12(5). The Division Bench held that once a tribunal's constitution is invalid, the award it passed cannot survive for some claims while staying intact for others, and set aside the award in full rather than only the parts LIC had chosen to challenge.
card_tip: A party resisting an award on Section 12(5) grounds should seek to set it aside in full; a party cannot keep an invalidly constituted tribunal's favourable findings while discarding the rest.
verification_notes: Parties, the 2019 unilateral arbitrator appointment, the Single Judge's Section 12(5) finding, the Division Bench's 6 October 2026 ruling, and the holding that the entire award falls once the tribunal's constitution is invalid are reported consistently by LiveLawBiz and Advocate Gandhi. The bench composition (Justices Anil Kshetarpal and Bharat Parashar) is as reported by LiveLawBiz.
